rationale: C22 is a direct predecessor concerning the prior White House Conference on Children and Youth. It supplies the later letter's core drafting machinery: presidentially calling the conference, appointing a national committee to direct it, and seeking active participation through the Governors and state-level bodies. C16 and C12 have secondary parallels involving youth-related advisory machinery and coordinated federal, state, local, and private participation, but neither matches the precise recurring conference framework as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am, therefore, directing that a sixth White House Conference on Children and Youth be held in March 1960.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I HAVE called a Midcentury White House Conference on Children and Youth
shared_material.explanation: Both presidential communications formally initiate the same recurring White House conference series.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Selection of the theme of the conference, as well as the responsibility for its direction, will be in the hands of a national advisory committee which I shall appoint soon.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: have appointed a committee of distinguished citizens to give general direction to the undertaking
shared_material.explanation: The later letter closely reuses the predecessor's committee-based direction of conference planning.

shared_material.child_excerpt: you should invite the Governors to participate actively at all stages, along with local officials from their States.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The value of this conference will depend upon full participation of each state... either you designate an existing body broadly representative in your state, or appoint a state committee to serve for this conference.
shared_material.explanation: Both use Governors as the mechanism for securing broad state participation in conference preparation.
